ios.desc:
Chumlord tracks how often you stay in touch with friends and family.

Add people to a roster (manually or from your contacts), set a catchup cadence per person (daily, weekly, monthly, custom, etc.), and log catchups when they happen. The main list splits into Scheduled and Coming Due. Coming Due is ranked by who merits attention most relative to their own cadence, so you can quickly triage who to reach out to first.

Each row shows the friend's avatar, cadence, next or last catchup date, and a health percentage from 0 to 100. Tap a row to edit, tap the calendar icon to schedule a date, swipe to text or snooze.
                                                                                                       
I created Chumlord as a passion project. No account, no server, no analytics. Everything stays on your device. Chumlord doesn't send notifications; you open it when you want to see where things stand.

quotes.text:
I made an app for iOS for creating a social roster and setting specific catchup cadences for each friend. It's free, is purely local and has no backend, and was co-created by my wife and I. We've gotten a lot of value out of it, and it has measurably improved our lives. Try it out if you're interested!

quotes.story_title: Americans' social activity has steeply declined in the past 30 years

quotes.text:
I built Chumlord, a little iOS app to help me stay in touch with the people I care about. Set a catchup cadence for each friend, and it shows you who you’re overdue to reach out to. No accounts, no data collection, just open it to check the health of your friend roster!

The app is technically trivial, but withering social circles is a topic I see routinely discussed on HN, and I decided I wanted to take a stab at giving the problem a physical form and a tool to shape it. Been using this for a week now, and I really like it!
